[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Amount: 10
- Contributor(s): Gary Teh
- Description: 10 minutes following up with Yuan Yuan at Blueprint (Bryan Johnson's 'Don't Die' longevity brand) - the first direct outreach to the Blueprint organisation, which the DAO's own dossier (BRYAN_JOHNSON_BLUEPRINT_DOSSIER.md) identifies as the archetypal Lane B / quantified-health buyer for cacao-as-measured-functional-input.
  
  LinkedIn connection flow: Yuan Yuan accepted Gary's friend request (Saturday 2:55 PM, 'I've accepted your friend request. Now let's chat!'). Gary's message Sunday 11:31 AM:
  
  'Glad to meet you. We have gourmet grade cacao supplies from the Amazon rainforest that have been heavy metal tested. And also options for flavonoid, thermobromine and caffeine content testing. Happy to make them available to supporters of BluePrint.'
  
  So the pitch made three distinct offers: (1) gourmet-grade Amazon rainforest cacao supply, (2) already heavy-metal tested, (3) optional/available testing for flavonoid, theobromine and caffeine content - explicitly positioned as making it available to Blueprint's SUPPORTERS (i.e. their customer base), not just to Blueprint procurement.
  
  WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE OUTREACH IN THE CACAO PIPELINE: Blueprint publishes a four-criterion public buying rubric for cocoa - 100% pure cocoa; un-dutched (no alkali); tested for heavy metals; high cocoa flavanols (Blueprint's own product carries 400+ mg flavanols per serving / 7.5% flavonols). Those four criteria are effectively the de facto spec of the quantified-health category, and all four are measurable - meaning an origin can either meet them or be correctly excluded. Blueprint has stated publicly that cocoa is 'one of the toughest products for our supply chain' and that they 'tested 10+ cocoa suppliers to find the cleanest one with the highest flavanols' - so they are actively source-hunting and are known to be hard to satisfy.
  
  ACCURACY FLAG for the record: the 'heavy metal tested' claim is defensible for the Oscar lot (14215834_gary_teh_oscar_lab_report.pdf: As, Cd, Pb and Cu by ICP-MS against ANVISA IN 160) but that report has NO Hg, NO OTA and NO flavonols. The flavonoid/theobromine/caffeine offer is correctly phrased as an available OPTION - results are not yet in hand; the CIC 6-metal and flavonoid panel requests were still outstanding as of the same day (see the 10-minute CIC follow-up logged immediately prior in this session). So do NOT represent flavanol numbers to Blueprint until CIC returns them - that is precisely the gate that decides this account.
  
  FORMAT MISMATCH to note: Blueprint buys COCOA POWDER (340 g pouches, 60-day supply), not ceremonial cacao in bags. The pitch language used is 'gourmet grade cacao supplies', which is Lane A/ceremonial language. Serving this account credibly requires powder-spec positioning (flavanols mg per serving, un-dutched proof, COA) rather than craft/ritual positioning. This is the Lane A vs Lane B distinction the DAO analysis warns not to merge.
  
  Open item: await Yuan Yuan's reply; have CIC flavanol + 6-metal results ready to attach as the qualifying document.
- Type: Time (Minutes)
--------
